paper.title: Adapting to Misspecification in Contextual Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: epsilon-misspecified contextual bandits with infinite actions and an online regression oracle (unknown misspecification)
unmapped: Mean loss mu(a,x) modelled semi-parametrically as <a, f(x)> with f in a class F mapping contexts to R^d; misspecification measured by the sequence-dependent average level eps_T(S), unknown to the learner
Learner has access to a (weighted) online square-loss regression oracle with regret Reg_Sq(T), and knows Reg_Sq(T)
Contexts and action sets A_t subset of the unit ball are chosen by an oblivious adversary; losses are stochastic in [-1,1] with time-invariant mean
settings.definition_quote: At each round t=1,...,T, the learner first observes a context x_t and an action set A_t subseteq A, where A subseteq R^d is a compact action space; ... A = {a: ||a|| <= 1} ... then observes a stochastic loss l_t in [-1,+1] ... the sequence of context vectors x_t and the associated sequence of action sets A_t are generated by an oblivious adversary.

settings.name_in_paper: misspecified linear contextual bandits with changing action sets (unknown misspecification)
unmapped: Misspecification measured by average level eps_T(S), unknown to the learner

settings.name_in_paper: misspecified contextual bandits with infinite actions, known misspecification bound
unmapped: The learner knows an upper bound eps on the average misspecification eps_T(S) (used to tune the learning rate)
Learner has an unweighted online square-loss regression oracle with regret Reg_Sq(T), known to the learner
settings.definition_quote:
Given a regression oracle $\SquareAlg$
  that satisfies \pref{ass:regression}, \infalg with
  learning rate $\gamma\propto\sqrt{dT/(\RegSquare+\veps)}$ guarantees
  that for all sequences $S$ with $\veps_T(S)\leq\veps$,
\begin{align*}
    \textstyle\Reg = \cO\left(\sqrt{dT\RegSquare}+ \veps\sqrt{d}T\right)\,.
\end{align*}

settings.name_in_paper: adversarial multi-armed bandit with M arms (master for bandit aggregation)
unmapped: Loss range [0,L] (L=2 in Corollary 2), known to the learner
settings.definition_quote: we work in a generic adversarial multi-armed bandit setting, at each time step, the agent selects an action A_t in [M], then observes a loss l_{t,A_t} in [0,L] for the action they selected.

algorithms.name: Corralling with SquareCB.Lin+ base algorithms and (1/2, 3/2 sqrt(dT Reg_Sq))-hedged Tsallis-INF master
Doubling-trick version of Algorithm 3 adapting to average dimension

symbols.Reg_Sq: regret bound Reg_Sq(T) of the online (weighted) square-loss regression oracle
symbols.eps_T: average misspecification level eps_T(S) of the context/action-set sequence

conditions: contexts and action sets chosen by an oblivious adversary
tuning: M = floor(log T) base instances with eps'_m = exp(-m)
master: (1/2, (3/2) sqrt(d T Reg_Sq))-hedged Tsallis-INF with eta = sqrt(1/(2T))

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: There exists an efficient reduction which, given access to a weighted regression oracle $\SquareAlg$ satisfying \pref{ass:weighted regression}, guarantees that for all sequences $S = (x_1,\cA_1),\ldots, (x_T,\cA_T)$, \Reg = \cO\left(\sqrt{dT\RegSquare \log(T)}+ \epsilon_T(S)\sqrt{d}T\right).

results.notes: No prior knowledge of misspecification. Per-step runtime O~(T_oracle + |A_t| poly(d)). Regret is pseudoregret against best action per round in A_t.

conditions: oblivious adversary for contexts and action sets
tuning: online Newton step as regression oracle (Reg_Sq = O(d log T))

source.label: cor:main
source.quote: Let $\cF=\{x\mapsto{}\theta\mid\theta \in \R^d,\nrm{\theta} \leq 1\}$. Then there exists an efficient algorithm that, for any sequence $S = (x_1,\cA_1),\ldots, (x_T,\cA_T)$, satisfies \Reg = \cO\left(d\sqrt{T}\log(T) + \epsilon_T(S)\sqrt{d}T\right).

results.notes: Resolves open problem of Lattimore et al.; matches their lower bound up to log factors.

symbols.Reg_Sq: regret bound of the online square-loss regression oracle
symbols.eps: known upper bound on the average misspecification eps_T(S)

source.label: thm:infinite
source.quote: Given a regression oracle $\SquareAlg$ that satisfies \pref{ass:regression}, \infalg with learning rate $\gamma\propto\sqrt{dT/(\RegSquare+\veps)}$ guarantees that for all sequences $S$ with $\veps_T(S)\leq\veps$, \Reg = \cO\left(\sqrt{dT\RegSquare}+ \veps\sqrt{d}T\right).

results.notes: Requires knowledge of eps via learning rate. Proposition 1 shows an approximate log-det-barrier solution computable in O~(|A_t| poly(d)) preserves the bound up to constants.

symbols.Reg_Sq: regret bound of the regression oracle
symbols.d_avg: average dimension (1/T) sum_t dim(A_t) of the action sets

tuning: doubling trick on sum of dim(A_t) on top of Algorithm 3

source.label: thm:sparse
source.quote: There exists an algorithm that, under the same conditions as \cref{thm:main}, satisfies $\Reg = \cO\left(\sqrt{\dbar T\RegSquare\log(T)}+\veps_T\sqrt{\dbar}T\right)$ without prior knowledge of $\dbar$ or $\veps_T$.

results.notes: Adapts to unknown d_avg and eps_T simultaneously.

symbols.stab_F: stability of potential F for the loss range
symbols.diam_F: diameter of potential F on the simplex
symbols.rho_1i: initial inverse probability of arm i
symbols.rho_Ti: expected max inverse probability of arm i up to T (inside expectation)
symbols.rho_1star: initial inverse probability of comparator arm
symbols.rho_Tstar: max inverse probability of comparator arm up to T (inside expectation)

source.label: thm:hedged ftrl
source.quote: For any potential $F$ with $\stab(F), \diam(F) < \infty$, the pseudo-regret ... for $(\alpha,R)$-hedged FTRL with learning rate $\eta =\sqrt{\diam(F)/(\stab(F)T)}$ is bounded by ... for all arms $a^*\in[M]$.

results.notes: Contains negative terms used to cancel importance-weighting costs; expectations over rho terms implicit. M arms mapped to K.

source.label: cor:Tsallis-INF
source.quote: Consider the adversarial multi-armed bandit problem with $M$ arms and losses $\tilde\ell_{t,m} \in [0,2]$. For any $\alpha\in(0,1)$ and $R>0$, the $(\alpha,R)$--hedged Tsallis-INF algorithm with learning rate $\eta=\sqrt{1/(2T)}$ guarantees that for all $\mstar\in\brk*{M}$, ... \leq 4\sqrt{2MT} + \E\left[\min\set{\frac{1}{1-\alpha},2\log(\rho_{T,\mstar })}M^\alpha -\rho_{T,\mstar}^\alpha \right]\cdot{}R

results.notes: M (number of base algorithms/arms) mapped to K. Losses in [0,2] rescale to bounded_01. Expectation applies to the bracketed term.

symbols.Reg_Sq: regret bound of the regression oracle
symbols.eps_T: average misspecification level of the full sequence S

conditions: algorithm run only on an obliviously chosen subset of timesteps

source.label: prop:anytime main thm
source.quote: Let $\cT \subset [T]$ be an obliviously chosen subset of timesteps. Then the upper bound from \cref{thm:main} on a sequence $S$ continues to hold if the algorithm is run on a sub-sequence $S_\cT$.

results.notes: Statement says the Theorem 1 bound continues to hold; the proof writes sqrt(d Reg_Sq log T) (missing T, likely a typo). Recorded as in the proof; intended bound equals Theorem 1.
